text:
mario: Heads up — p95 latency jumped from ~160ms -> ~420ms on a subset of hosts after the v3.4 model swap rolled at 09:12. Suspect token-scheduler thrashing + kernel rebinds. KV cache hit rate on affected shards fell 78% -> 46%. Anyone else seeing this?
perf-bot: deploy v3.4 to cluster-asia completed at 09:12 (rollout r-202603-34).
anya: seeing it too. p50 looks fine but p95/p99 are flaring and throughput is down ~18% on that node pool. :eyes: tagging @kai for kernel selection traces.
kai: pulling traces now. initial look: many requests are getting bound to quantized-kernel then mid-request jumping to fp16 because seq len crosses the threshold — repeated kernel rebinds per request (thrash). Batcher fallback hysteresis also kicking in.
devon: KV hit drop correlates with eviction spikes. Evict rate 3x in same window. My hunch: tokenizer change increased unique prefix variety -> less KV reuse.
mario: confirmed — diffing token maps between v3.3 and v3.4 shows token boundary shifts for long prompts; avg tokens/msg +12% on canary traffic.
kai: sample log snippet: ```kernel_bind: quantized_v2 -> fp16_v1 | seq_len: 512 -> 768 | reason: seq_overflow```
devon: simple mitigation idea: add temporary hysteresis so the batcher holds a kernel binding for N ms to avoid flip-flop. Can patch canary traffic quickly.
mario: go for it if it helps, but we should also consider KV-warmup for users hit by tokenizer changes.
anya: +1. Also pin tokenizer mapping for canary to avoid mixed encodings during rollout.
devon: applied patch to canary (20% traffic): `batcher.hysteresis_ms=1000`. Monitoring dashboards: https://redwood.infra/dashboards/runtime-rollout
perf-bot: Alert update — p95 on canary reduced from ~420ms -> ~210ms in the 5min window after patch.
kai: good signal. Action items: (1) add metric `kernel_rebinds_per_request`, (2) add `kv_prefetch_warmup` step for tokenization-affecting rollouts, (3) run synthetic long-seq workload to reproduce and validate.
mario: also adding rollout checklist rule: if tokenizer surface change >5% or avg tokens/msg delta >8% => require KV warmup + bind-pin canary to a single kernel.
anya: I'll open a PR to add checklist + update release notes. Filing postmortem after rollout stabilizes.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-045; assignees: @mario @kai @devon @anya.
mario: thanks team. keep short updates here — if we see re-regression we rollback the model immediately. :thumbsup:
